sources.entry: DockAnchor - Lock the macOS Dock to a single screen in a multi-monitor setup. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/bwya77/DockAnchor) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: DockAnchor is a macOS app that keeps the Dock pinned to one chosen display in a multi-monitor setup instead of letting it jump to whichever screen the cursor reaches.
summary.what_it_does: DockAnchor intercepts mouse movement events with a low-level event tap and blocks the Dock from moving to secondary displays, rather than killing and restarting the Dock. You pick an anchor display, and it can auto-move the Dock there when protection starts. It detects monitors as they connect, disconnect, or move, and falls back to the primary display if the anchor is removed. Additional features include profiles with automatic switching based on connected displays, a virtual monitor view, cursor position offset settings, a menu bar icon showing protection status, start at login, and light/dark/system themes. It requires macOS Accessibility permission to function.
use_cases: keep the Dock on one monitor
pin Dock to primary or built-in display
switch dock settings by connected monitors
how_to_run: Alternatively, download the Apple signed app from the Releases page
Building from source: open DockAnchor.xcodeproj in Xcode, build and run, then grant Accessibility permission
notable: Prevents dock movement at the system event level without restarting the Dock, so no flashing or app interruption
Profiles that can switch automatically based on which displays are connected
Virtual monitor display that updates in real time as monitors change
Auto fallback to the primary display when the anchor display is disconnected
Installable via Homebrew cask or a signed release download
caveats: Requires Accessibility permission; without it the core feature does not work
